title: Dynamics 365 Knowledge Management - Simply Explained

entities.name: Mirko Peters
entities.quote: I'm Mirko Peters from M365FM, and this is a Microsoft Knowledge Nugget.

entities.name: Dynamics 365
entities.quote: That's where Dynamics 365 Knowledge Management comes in.

entities.name: Dynamics 365 Customer Service
entities.quote: This ties directly into the work agents already do in Dynamics 365 customer service.

quotes.text: If one agent explains a return policy one way, and another gives a different version, the customer doesn't see an internal knowledge problem. They see a company that can't agree with itself.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows from the customer's view why consistent, shared answers matter.

quotes.text: A knowledge base becomes the company's working memory, keeping useful know how available when someone takes leave, changes jobs, joins the team, or simply forgets a detail during a busy afternoon.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable framing of a knowledge base as organisational memory.

quotes.text: A case tells the agent what happened, and a knowledge article helps them decide what to do next.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains concisely how cases and articles work together.

quotes.text: A team can publish hundreds of articles and still leave agents searching. Volume isn't the goal. Useful current answers are the goal, and that takes regular review, clear ownership, and feedback from people doing the work.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear recommendation that quality and ownership beat article volume.

chapters.title: The problem: answers in people's heads
Why teams need a shared knowledge base
The life of a knowledge article
Finding knowledge while helping a customer
Keeping knowledge accurate, safe and useful

takeaways: A shared knowledge base gives every support agent the same approved answers, so customers get consistent responses on every channel.
Knowledge articles move through a lifecycle of drafting, labelling, expert review, approval, publishing to the right audience and regular updates.
Clear titles, an owner per article, permissions and feedback from agents and search misses keep the knowledge base useful.
hook: Support agents waste time hunting through old emails and spreadsheets while customers wait, and different agents give different answers. This episode shows customer service teams how Dynamics 365 Knowledge Management turns scattered know-how into approved, searchable articles inside daily case work. You will learn how articles are created, reviewed, found and kept current.
